calls.head: Unstoppable force, meet immovable object
calls.body: The Senators are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Bruins are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Senators’ chance quality wins out.

calls.head: There’s no curse: Swayman against the Senators
calls.body: Swayman has been shaky against the Senators since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Swayman starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .863 against the Senators.

calls.head: Stay out of the box, Bruins
calls.body: The Senators’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Bruins’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Bruins more than most. The Bruins take a lot of penalties and the Senators draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

BOS.head: We gave Boston only a 35% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 65% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Boston found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Boston usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Ottawa usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Boston’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.0% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: The Senators take down the Bruins
paras: Tim Stützle scored midway through the first and again less than two minutes later to put the Senators up 2-0. Drake Batherson and Michael Amadio scored a little over four minutes apart early in the second to make it 4-0. Samuel Ersson took over from Linus Ullmark in net for Ottawa to start the third. James Hagens got the Bruins on the board early in the third. Stützle added an assist for a three-point night.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Jeremy Swayman stopped 20 of 24 for the Bruins.

Three players picked up ten-minute misconducts. Neither power play scored: the Senators killed all four Bruins power plays, and the Bruins killed all four of Ottawa’s. The Bruins killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes late in the first. The Sens moved to 2-0-0, and the Bruins dropped to 2-2-0.

items.text: Tim Stützle passed Wade Redden for sixth on the Senators’ all-time scoring list, with 413 points.
Claude Giroux’s five-game point streak against Boston ended.
None of the preview’s three calls held.
